gaps.category: Small food producers and horeca hygiene/allergen duties (FASFC notification, autocontrole, sector guides)
gaps.first_search: FAVV autocontrole gids G-040 horeca bakkerij meldingsplicht allergenen traceerbaarheid kleine zaak
gaps.why: Belgium has a very large number of small food operators: bakeries, snack bars, frituren, caterers and farm shops. The FASFC notification, the autocontrole guide (G-040 for horeca and others), the allergen duties, and the controls and fee system (retributie) all fall on them. Only butchers were covered. Horeca GKS was rejected as a cash-register issue, and the hygiene workflow itself was not checked.

gaps.category: Environmental permits and annual reports for small Class 2/3 firms (VLAREM meldingen, Walloon permis d'environnement, Brussels permis d'environnement)

gaps.why: Garages, car washes, small workshops and farms must notify or renew environmental permits and keep records. Permit expiry dates and municipal notifications hit many small firms at once. Only F-gas, tanks and waste were checked, and only for Flanders. Wallonia and Brussels were barely covered.

gaps.category: Self-employed and sole-trader obligations: sociale verzekeringsfonds contributions, BTW (VAT) small-business exemption regime (kleine ondernemingen), Belgian VAT listing and intrastat
gaps.first_search: btw vrijstellingsregeling kleine ondernemingen 2025 2026 aangifte klantenlisting kleine ondernemer; franchise TVA petites entreprises 2025 déclaration
gaps.why: Sole traders and family firms are the biggest buyer group. The VAT franchise regime for small businesses (vrijstellingsregeling, reformed in 2025), quarterly VAT returns, annual client listings and Intrastat are recurring mandatory filings. General accounting is out of scope, but the specific small-firm filings and the 2025-2026 changes were not examined.

gaps.category: Taxi, VTC, private hire and small driver-transport licensing (Brussels taxi/LVC reform, Walloon taxi decree) and the Brussels/Flemish low-emission zone (LEZ) vehicle rules for small fleets

gaps.why: K23 covers only Flemish taxis and was rejected for one-off licensing. Brussels has a separate taxi and LVC regime, and since 2024 a reform of the Brussels taxi rules. LEZ derogations and fleet renewals affect many one-van tradespeople, a group with large numbers of small operators. Row 18 was marked 'not searched separately'.

gaps.category: Pharmacies and health-professional compliance (FAGG reporting, medicine traceability, Belgian pharmacist reporting, RIZIV/INAMI) plus new mandatory e-health duties for small practices

Service vouchers are the alternative. Covered by social secretariats and the Dimona/DmfA and PAB ideas: nothing new beyond K15 and K22.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No Belgian police purchase-register rule found (search returned only Dutch law). Scrap dealers who collect or trade waste in Flanders must register with OVAM and keep a daily-updated digital waste register for 5 years (VLAREMA). One candidate (C01). Wallonia and Brussels not checked.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Could not confirm any current Belgian police-register duty for second-hand dealers; results were French and Dutch law. Only the 1993 ambulant-trade law and the 1987 precious-metals law surfaced. Pawnbrokers not reached in any search. Marked unverified.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Buyers of precious metals must be in the waarborgregister at the Royal Mint (law of 11 Aug 1987), need a clean criminal record extract and a verified scale, display buy prices, and are capped at EUR 3,000 cash per transaction. A news.belgium.be item on cash limits for gold dealers could not be fetched (403). Small group. One weak candidate (C02).

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Depollution/dismantling centres need regional approval (OVAM, Wallonia, Brussels) with an initial and yearly follow-up inspection (Vinçotte), plus Febelauto affiliation to issue destruction certificates. Daily waste register also applies (see C01). No dismantler-specific software found. One weak candidate (C03).

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Belgian transporters must register animal movements in Sanitel within 7 days and keep a transporter register plus cleaning/disinfection registers; transporter licences come from Animal Welfare (Flanders) and the FASFC. DGZ Veeportaal is free and DGZ keys documents for a fee. One weak candidate (C04). Rules possibly changed with the 2022 royal decrees; unchecked.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Butchers must run an autocontrole/HACCP system under the royal decree of 14 Nov 2003; sector guide G-003 and the generic FASFC practice handbook G-044 apply. Consultancies (Kiwa, LRQA) sell guidance; no butcher-specific registration software found. One weak candidate (C05).

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: All beekeepers must be registered with the FASFC and report notifiable bee diseases (royal decree of 7 Mar 2007); more than 24 hives counts as professional. Hobby-heavy, low willingness to pay. Nothing worth a candidate beyond a note.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K10 (antibiotic registration, rejected). Not searched further.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Flanders: abstractions of 500 m3/yr or more pay the VMM groundwater levy, farmers declare by 15 March through the free VMM heffingenloket, new or stopped abstractions are notified within 2 months, flow metering required. Free state portal covers the filing. Drillers: nothing new beyond K07. One weak candidate (C06).

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K06. Flemish waste transporters must register through the OVAM Webloket; no software gap found.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Lift owners must have periodic inspections by approved bodies (Vinçotte, Kiwa) and risk analyses for lifts over 15 years; Brussels uses approved SECT bodies. Regional rules for Wallonia and Flanders not confirmed. Buyer is mostly syndics: nothing new beyond K03. Boilers and pressure equipment not searched.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: No Flemish source found on private wells used for drinking or food production; results were Dutch. Marked unverified. Own abstractions are covered by the VMM notification (see C06).

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K05 and K16. Not searched.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Flemish temp agencies need regional approval under the decree on private employment mediation (BVR of 10 Dec 2010) with a code of conduct draft approved July 2025; no annual reporting duty confirmed. Large agencies and social-secretariat tools dominate. Nothing new beyond K01, K02, K17.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K09 (eLys, rejected). Not searched.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Small vzw/ASBL file annual accounts with the enterprise court (large ones with the National Bank), keep a UBO registration, and give volunteers a declaration of honour with 2026 caps of EUR 44.02/day and EUR 1,760.83/year. A 2018 plan to make filing universal and add a register of gifts above EUR 3,000 could not be confirmed as law. One weak candidate (C07). Halal/kosher supervision not searched.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Covered only through livestock transporters (C04) and the known taxi idea K23. No new small-fleet duty found; not searched separately.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Flanders abolished the prior ambulant-trade authorisation from 1 Apr 2024 (KBO registration suffices); Brussels needs a KBO registration for door-to-door sales. Bureaux de change register with the FSMA under the royal decree of 27 Dec 1994, but current rules and reporting were not confirmed. Nothing candidate-worthy.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Childcare (Flanders): daily attendance register kept 12 months, monthly attendance to Opgroeien by the 7th via free AARON or own IT via web service, fiscal and income-tariff attests via Mijn Opgroeien (C08). Driving schools: Flemish approval with per-site permit, EUR 342 fee, changes by form (C09). Hunting: WBEs file the annual wildrapport and apply for the large-game cull plan before 15 Sept (C10). Tattoo studios: no Belgian source found (results Dutch). Small food producers: only the butcher guidance (C05). Walloon ONE childminder duties: nothing current found.

result.competitor: KoudSmart by OutSmart (https://out-smart.com/features/koudsmart): Dutch-language digital F-gas logbook per installation that records refrigerant charge, top-ups and removals, cylinder stock, unit-linked leak checks and automatic F-gas reports, with a work order raised after a positive leak result. Its page does not mention Belgium/Flemish rules or the relative-leakage calculation. Joblogic (UK) has an F-gas logbook in its mobile field-service app. Leaklog (Slovakia) is an electronic circuit logbook with QR labels and operator access. Climalife's F-Gas Solutions is a free app for leak-check frequency and GWP calculations. EFCTC offers a free Excel logbook. In France, Extractivs does CERFA forms, which do not fit Belgium. Large players such as Engie Cofely have run in-house digital logbooks since 2010. Found no free state portal; VEKA says there is no online portal.
result.duty: Confirmed (Flanders). Companies that install, maintain, repair or decommission stationary cooling installations with F-gases need a Flemish approval (annual fee EUR 145 in 2026, at least one approved technician, inspection by an approved inspection body), and they must fill in the installation-bound logbook completely and correctly. VLAREM II art. 5.16.3.3 applies to classified installations of 5 kW or more, including air conditioners and heat pumps. The relative leakage must be calculated and noted after each top-up, with a maximum of 5% a year, and leaks above 5% must be repaired within 14 days (Frixis). The EU leak-check frequencies come from Regulation (EU) 2024/573 art. 7. Wallonia has a similar framework: the AGW of 12 July 2007, amended in 2012, for systems of at least 12 kW or more than 3 kg, with an Annex III company register. The Flemish approval page notes that no active inspection body in Flanders currently issues the European certificate. Not checked: the Brussels rules and the exact penalties.
result.market: Not reached. Flanders publishes a list of approved cooling companies (datasets.omgeving.vlaanderen.be PDF), but the fetch returned HTTP 503, and no published count was found in Dutch searches. Operators (shops, restaurants, butchers) are numerous, but the legal logbook duty in practice runs through the approved contractor, so the realistic paying buyer is the contractor. My guess, unverified: a few hundred to low thousands of firms in Flanders.
result.reason: The duty is real. Approved Flemish cooling companies must keep a full installation-bound logbook, and VLAREM II art. 5.16.3.3 covers classified installations of 5 kW or more, including air conditioners and heat pumps. The claim of no competitor is wrong. OutSmart's KoudSmart, a Dutch-language field-service module, already provides a digital F-gas logbook per installation, links leak checks to each unit, raises repair work orders, tracks cylinders and produces F-gas reports. Joblogic, Leaklog, Climalife's free F-Gas Solutions app and the free EFCTC template cover parts of the job. The only gap is the Flanders-specific relative-leakage calculation and the report to Handhaving (enforcement), which KoudSmart's page does not mention. That gap is too thin for a standalone product. Buyers are a few hundred to a few thousand approved firms (count not reached).

The duty is real. OVAM's page says collectors, waste traders and brokers must update a digital register every working day and keep it 5 years. It lists the fields: date, EURAL code, tonnes, carrier, processor. The page states no penalty. A search result says OVAM offers a standard Excel template for this register, but I did not open the template page. That weakens willingness to pay, since a free template already covers the basic job. No Belgium-specific scrap-yard software turned up, but the search was thin and weighbridge/waste-ERP vendors probably cover it. I found no current count of registered businesses. One old OVAM study suggests thousands, mixed with carriers. Registered yards are a niche, EVOA/MATIS reporting is a separate duty, and Wallonia and Brussels were not checked. Pain is moderate and the market is small.

Duty confirmed on the current DGZ page. Movement documents must be registered in Sanitel within 7 days, with the document kept 5 years. A cleaning and disinfection register is kept 3 years. Walloon transport authorisation is valid 5 years. Veeportaal is a free state-linked tool for movement registration. DGZ offers a paid paper service. I found no third-party hauler software. The market is small and niche, and I found no count of Belgian transporters. The register is a simple form, so there is little pain, and the hauler or farmer can use free Veeportaal. Willingness to pay is likely low. I did not check for a Veeportaal API or bulk upload. I did not verify the 2022 royal decrees.

result.reason: The duty is real. The Royal Decree of 14 Nov 2003 requires HACCP-based autocontrol and traceability. Butchers follow guide G-003, and FASFC handbook G-044 covers B2C sectors. It is continuous, with FASFC inspections. I did not check the penalty. Competition already covers the core job. Generic HACCP and temperature-logging apps are sold in Belgium: Holifresh (Belgian, Mont-Saint-Guibert), Alcomo HACCP (claims use in Belgium), Hygiène Expert and Flowtify. Normec HACCPro is Dutch-oriented. Kiwa/Vinçotte sell consultancy and certification. I found no butcher-specific Belgian app, so a niche G-003 product might exist, but the tool is crowded, price-sensitive and sold into a shrinking market. About 3,432 independent butchers and delis existed in 2018, per NSZ via RetailDetail (2019). Small abattoirs were not screened. The paid-product pricing and the FASFC penalty were not checked.

The duties are real. Small vzw's must file annual accounts with the enterprise court (the National Bank only above thresholds). Within 30 days of approval, so a calendar-year vzw files by 30 July. Annual UBO re-confirmation is mandatory, with sanctions of EUR 250 to 50,000 per Jubel and Crowe. Volunteer-expense declarations also apply. A 2024 IBR study found about 1 in 3 very small vzw's don't file. I found no dedicated compliance-calendar software. UBO confirmation is free on MyMinfin. Weak points: volunteer-run buyers, low willingness to pay, accountants and federations (VSDC) cover the need, and the universal-filing bill is unconfirmed. I did not check vendor products by name or the market size from the register.

Duty is real. Since 1 Jan 2026 EU sanctions require polished-diamond importers (stones of 0.5 ct or more) to provide a Due Diligence Statement on Diamond Origin with each import. Rough imports of mixed origin need a Kimberley Process certificate listing all origin countries. Belgian FPS Economy has run spot checks since May 2026, and goods can be blocked. I did not find the penalty level. AWDC gives members a free DDS template and a step-by-step plan. Tracr and Everledger already supply traceability records. The market is small: 1,470 active Antwerp diamond firms, over half of them small. The duty is a letter of attestation plus record-keeping, so the pain and willingness to pay are low. A niche tool for logging supplier origin evidence is possible, but a free template and a small, tight-knit buyer base limit it.

The supplier duty is only a draft. A March 2026 VRT article says "binnenkort", and I found no adopted decree or start date. The Minaraad/SERV questioned whether it is needed. The duty is a once-a-year address list for VEKA, with fines mentioned up to EUR 50,000. That is simple to export from existing dealer ERP or routing software, so there is little recurring pain. The buyer group is tiny and fragmented, and willingness to pay is low. A Dutch search found no niche product built for this, but I could not confirm competitors. Dealer count not found. The existing installer-reporting duty, with fines up to EUR 20,000, falls on installers, not dealers.

Duty is real: Brussels hosts must register with Brussels Economie et Emploi before operating, then with Brussels Fiscalite within 31 days. The fine is EUR 1,000 per unit. A monthly declaration is filed on MyTax, and a regional tax applies. Flanders requires aanmelding (over 29,700 aangemelde logies, undated). Wallonia tourist tax is communal (by rol per the model regulation), so it is fragmented and not a filing flow. No Belgian software specific to this found, but I didn't search PMS or channel managers. Weak points: the official MyTax portal does the filing, the Brussels bottleneck is the urban-planning certificate that software can't fix, Airbnb collects some data itself, and hosts are scattered. Wallonia has no uniform filing, so a unified kit is thin. Not checked: police guest register, Flemish entry-into-force date, and the Brussels host count (about 2,500 non-compliant listings per VRT).

result.duty: Belgian AML law of 18 Sep 2017 plus the BIV AML regulation (in force since 1 Jul 2022): client due diligence, written risk analysis, suspicious-transaction reports to CTIF-CFI.
result.market: Not counted. The page does not say how many agents there are. The claim cites 334 agents inspected in 2021, which is a sample, not the full register.
result.reason: The duty is real: the AML law of 18 Sep 2017 and the BIV AML regulation in force since 1 Jul 2022 cover buyer and tenant checks, written risk analysis and reports to CTIF. But the core job is already done by antiwitwas.be. That is a paid, subscription-based tool for BIV agents, sized by office, and approved by FOD Economie. It has client and counterparty screening, client and transaction risk scoring, a guided wizard, CTIF reporting and a 10-year record. A search result says using the BIV tools gives a presumption of compliance, so a rival product has to beat an endorsed incumbent. I did not check pricing, other vendors or a market count. The 2021 inspection figures came from the claim and I did not re-verify them.

Duty is real: wallonie.be says a class 3 declaration lasts 10 years and must be renewed on expiry, after a change to the class 3 list, or on a move. Sanctions are administrative (formal notice, suspension) and penal fines. No operator-side expiry tracker found; only commune tools (the SPW "Déclarations" tool, Urb@web with alerts). Weak product: a 10-year cycle is very infrequent, the free Mon Espace form already does the filing, and the buyer is a scattered group of micro-firms with little willingness to pay. Market size was not checked, and the pending permit reform is unconfirmed. The wallonie.be page does not make clear whether the 10-year validity is a maximum.
